### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 ran early in every trace (median relative position about 0.39), A25 ran just after them (median about 0.44), and A19, A21, A24 and A29 ran late (medians about 0.67–0.70). In the later window, A19, A21 and A24 run early (medians about 0.34–0.36), A29 runs between the groups (median about 0.59), and A25 runs just before A20, A22 and A23 (median about 0.38 versus their 0.65). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]

- Pairwise relations show near-complete order reversals while the activities still occur together in essentially every trace: A20 preceded A25 in about 98 in 100 traces before, and A25 precedes A20 in all traces after; A19 moved from after A20, A22 and A23 (about 31 in 100 traces) to before them (about 44 in 100); A21 and A24 flipped the same way (for example, A22 preceded A21 in about 38 in 100 traces before, while A21 precedes A22 in about 29 in 100 after); A29, which previously followed A20, A22 and A23 in about 99–100 in 100 traces, now precedes them in about 98 in 100. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL028]

- Successors moved with the reorder. A19, A21 and A24 led to A30 in about 97–99 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions before; in the later window they lead to A25 in about 95–100 in 100, and A30 is no longer among their observed successors. Conversely, A20, A22 and A23 sent about 30–39 in 100 of their outgoing transitions to A25 before, while now A30 receives about 32–34 in 100 and A25 has nearly disappeared from their successors. A29 now leads mainly to A20, A22 and A23 (about 30–33 in 100 each) where it previously led to A21, A19 and A24. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]

- Step distances shifted consistently: the gap from A29 to A30 grew from about 2 steps (97 in 100 cases) to about 4 steps (94 in 100), and the gap from A40 to A25 shrank from about 4 steps (90 in 100) to 2–3 steps. [LAG004, LAG007]

- A02 became much more frequent: it appeared in about 8 in 100 traces before and about 34 in 100 after (mean occurrences per trace 0.08 to 0.35), it now sits early (median relative position about 0.33), precedes A19 in about 13 in 100 traces (about 1 in 100 before), and its outgoing transitions go mainly to A19, A24 and A21. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL001]

- Participation and repetition also shifted: A19 now appears in about 44 in 100 traces (about 31 before) and A21 in about 29 in 100 (about 38 before); A41, present in every trace in both windows, is executed more often per trace (about 1.5 to about 1.8) and repeats within a trace in about 40 in 100 traces versus about 33 before. [POS002, POS004, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two groups of activities reversed their execution order: the sequence A19, A21, A24 — together with A29 and A25 — which previously ran after A20, A22 and A23, now runs before them, and A30, which previously followed A19, A21 and A24, now follows A20, A22 and A23. The order reversals are near-complete in pairs that still co-occur in every trace, and the position of every involved activity shifted in the direction the reversal predicts. [REL010, REL017, REL024, REL025, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

The rearrangement appears consistently in three views of the same behaviour — pairwise order, successor choices at the group boundaries, and step distances — rather than in a single indicator. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG004, LAG007]

The volume of qualifying evidence also far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 58 control-flow items against fewer than one expected without a change. [screening]

Limitations: the indicators capture event order and relative positions, not clock time, so the change is established in ordering terms only. The evidence also cannot fully rule out that the two windows sample different pre-existing variants at shifted frequencies rather than a reordering within one flow, although within each window the orders are almost perfectly consistent, which a pure variant-mix shift would struggle to explain. [REL017, REL024, REL025]

Other differences: A02, observed in about 8 in 100 traces before, now appears in about 34 in 100, sits at the head of the earlier group and leads mainly to A19, A24 and A21 [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL001, REL003]; A40 now leads mainly to A02, A19, A21 and A24 where it previously led to A20, A22 and A23 [DIR009]; A41 is executed more often per trace and repeats in more traces [OCC002]; and within the swapped groups A19 appears in more traces (about 31 to 44 in 100) while A21 appears in fewer (about 38 to 29 in 100) [POS002, POS004].
